# Bs walks into a home, hearth & real estate firm

Somewhere right now, in a home, hearth & real estate office, someone is doing exactly what the myths describe — and has never heard of **Bs**. This file is the introduction.

## Before the Office, the Story

**The Mask of the Midwife.** In the birth-chamber, the midwife donned the Bes-mask and danced his dance; his grimace drew the malign spirits’ attention onto himself and away from mother and child.  The Beset-amulets and the ‘Bes-chamber’ scenes of Deir el-Medina show the rite in domestic detail.

**The Dwarf Who Amuses the Gods.** The Westcar Papyrus’ wonder-tale of the dwarf Dedi, who dances and performs before the court, is read as Bes’ narrative shadow — the small deformed being whose skill and humour carry more power than the great.  Bes never speaks in the texts; he dances.

## The Reveal, Seat by Seat

### Home, Hearth & Real Estate

*The household god without a temple — every home was his, at the bed, the door, the mirror.* The match is not poetic license. Strip the trade to its function and the function is the myth.

### Wedding, Family & Maternity

*Guardian of the birth-chamber — the midwife's mask and the nursery's ward are his.* Nobody in that trade worships at this temple. They just keep its hours.

### Insurance & Protection Services

Now read the why-line with the office in mind: *The protector of the threshold — apotropaic insurance in dwarf-form, premium paid in amulets.* The people doing this work did not borrow the archetype. They re-derived it — the way Bs was always going to be re-derived wherever protection, childbirth, joy matters.

## Not the First Rebrand

Bes is the great syncretic absorber of the late period: Pantheos-Bes carries the attributes of all gods.  The Greeks equated him with their own apotropaic dwarves and the Pataikos figures, and Roman soldiers carried his amulets across the empire — the household god travelled as military gear. The office is only the latest translation.
